text:
The week opens on a good note: Monday at Groundwork, Jordan makes real progress on Coda, the practice-log app they've been noodling on for months, getting the streak counter and its little animated flames working. There's a clear-eyed observation about needing that specific environment — the noise, the anonymity, the coffee — to actually get things done, versus the couch-and-feeds spiral at home. Pepper does her doorway ritual, dinner is quiet, and the day earns a small note of gratitude for its uneventfulness.

Wednesday breaks that calm. Marcus announces a coming restructuring in standup, delivered casually but landing hard — the team of six may get split up. Lena, rattled by her third reorg in two years, tells Jordan she's already job-hunting and done rebuilding trust with new managers each time. Jordan, 14 months in and on their second reorg already, doesn't blame her, and notes the irony that the first reorg actually improved things by moving them onto internal tools — the very team now at risk of dissolving. Rather than go home, Jordan stays late doing low-stakes busywork (cleaning old Figma files), naming it directly as avoidance rather than productivity. The evening ends deflated — cereal for dinner, Pepper asleep, portfolio update deferred to "maybe this weekend."

Friday shifts the tone again. A run with Mika at Greenwood Park — golden light, three miles, the usual dynamic of her pulling ahead and looping back — becomes the emotional turn of the week. Jordan tells her about the restructuring, and she delivers the week's sharpest insight: that Jordan retreats from Coda whenever work gets unstable, and returns to it when they need to feel better — that Coda might functionally already be the portfolio update Jordan's been avoiding. Jordan recognizes the truth in this immediately. The evening ends with a small, symbolic act of follow-through: 20 minutes fixing a color contrast issue on Coda before bed, explicitly framed as small but countable.

Saturday closes the week on a deliberately uneventful note — errands, a new green rug that Pepper claims immediately, a real dinner cooked and eaten at the table instead of the couch, an old movie chosen for its unobtrusiveness. Minor chaos at 2am courtesy of Pepper and a water glass. Jordan calls the day "not notable" and seems at peace with that.

Across the week, a pattern surfaces that Mika names explicitly: work instability triggers avoidance (busywork, screen time, deferral), while Coda and small domestic rituals — Pepper, cooking, the new rug — serve as counterweights. The portfolio update remains undone. The reorg's actual shape and timeline are still unknown, Lena's job search is underway while Jordan hasn't started one, and whether Jordan will sustain the post-Mika momentum on Coda into next week is left open.
